title: Global manager layer - first-class cross-project PM addon
description: EPIC BRIEF. Build the global manager as a top-level addon: a machine-level project-management layer over any number of linked Boreal workspaces - kanban boards, a capture inbox, and a ranked cross-project next queue - for both the human owner and PM agents. Full design: docs/product/GLOBAL_MANAGER_DESIGN.md (read it before claiming any child task). Governing invariant: the global layer owns exactly three kinds of state - the registry (linked projects and lifecycle), global records (portfolio containers and genuinely project-less items), and regenerable freshness-stamped rollup caches - and projects everything else from workspace truth. It never stores or mirrors project truth; a global view that can disagree with a project about that project has failed. Sprint-to-phase map: sprint G1 is phase 0 registry lifecycle and link or delink; sprint G2 is the independent packaging track (distributable binary, install.sh, homebrew prep); sprint G3 is phase 1 reference URIs (hard-blocked on the directive hardening sprint because it touches core record types); sprint G4 is phase 2 rollup contract and aggregation; sprint G5 is phase 3 global capture and triage; sprint G6 is phase 4 aggregate next and aging signals; sprint G7 is phase 5 portfolio containers; sprint G8 is phase 6 the honest kanban board. Non-goals: no mirrored project truth, no second workflow engine at global level, no multi-user sync in v1 (but URIs and registry ids must be designed to survive it per docs/architecture/V2_STORAGE_COLLABORATION_PLAN.md), and the console stays a thin layer that renders CLI JSON and writes only through command contracts. Process rule learned from the last epic: every implementation task here carries a declared done-gate of pnpm check - evidence must record that exact command with a passing outcome or the task cannot close.
acceptanceCriteria: All seven sprint containers under this milestone are closed with recorded commit checkpoint SHAs
A second repo can be linked, appear on the global board with fresh rollups, receive a routed inbox item, and be delinked without any write to that repo
bwrk global next returns a ranked directive per linked project sourced from rollups
On a bare machine install with no registry, the first bwrk global command bootstraps the addon interactively and via typed error in json mode
